item.title: Rick Hyde - PencilBooth Take #1
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde

Hello, and welcome to my very first newsletter!


And what a monumental event to be a part of. Much like when The Sex Pistols played at Manchester's Lesser Free Trade Hall in June 1976, people will say, “I swear I was there” at the conception of this email correspondence. Or more likely, they won’t. But hey, I’m glad to have you onboard nonetheless. In fact I’m thrilled that anyone has subscribed to this at all. So in that spirit, may I wish you all a very warm welcome, and extend a great big thank you for your support and interest in All Tomorrow’s Pixels, and my creative journey.

You say goodbye, and I say hello, hello, hello

I should also point out, at this early stage of proceedings, that I have been collecting subscribers through my website for the past 7 or 8 years now. Admittedly, it’s taken me a while to get my first email out, but what can I say… Good things come to those who wait!

  If however, you’ve lost all memory of subscribing, did so in a state of high intoxication, or simply have major subscription regrets, simply scroll to the bottom of this take and hit unsubscribe. Spams not my jam.  

Right, now that’s dealt with, let’s get on with the show. Fingers crossed, there’s still a few of you left!

A bit about me

It feels only appropriate, that I give myself a little introduction.

  My name is Rick. I’m an illustrator, animator and designer from Manchester, England.

  First thing to say about myself is I love the 60s (and early 70s). I dig it, to coin the phrase. I love the music, the fashion, the movies, the pop culture.


And that’s what fuels my work. All that delicious 60s psychedelia, jumbled up with the comic books and cartoons I grew up on, and a tonne of other stuff from my everyday life.


All Tomorrow’s Pixels, is of course, a homage to one of my all time favourite bands from that period, The Velvet Underground, and their song “All Tomorrow's Parties”.


I mainly create art digitally though, so I’m no purist. I guess what I’m trying to do is create a modern take on all that old gold. Bridge the gap between contemporary, commercial accessibility and retrospective nostalgia. That’s the theory anyway.


Right, on with the news…

Choreus

February was a big month for me for two reasons. Firstly I was offered a place in the artist directory on Choreus, by the wonderful people at The Jacky Winter Group. Choreus is an innovative platform, that offers flexible artist representation. It’s a fresh take on the traditional model, where the artist decides the terms, length and type of help needed on each project, and I’m made up to be onboard!

Taco Bell x Fast Company

The second big thing that happened in February was getting an editorial gig with Fast Company! I was asked to create a series of 14 sidebar spot illustrations, for a story on Taco Bell. The article is featured in the latest (March/April 2024) issue of the magazine, and discusses Taco Bell’s strategy for global cultural domination, under the leadership of new CEO, Sean Tresvant. Big thanks to Alice Alves at Fast Company for bringing me on board, and for the great art direction. Click here to view the whole project.

Spinspiration

This section is all about what sounds are on high rotation in ATP studio. Recently I’ve been listening to the fantastic compilation - Music For The Stars (Celestial Music 1960-1979). Released on the Two-Piers label, it’s a collection of laid back, late night songs. From English psych-tinged folk to the 60’s West Coast scene, there’s plenty in here to loose yourself to. I’ve loved absorbing it’s soulful sounds and sonic beauty whilst scribbling away on the iPad. Why not give it a listen?

Eye candy

I was debating calling this The Retrospection Section, but I’m running with Eye Candy for now (not me, the book). It’s a little look at what books, magazines and ephemera, from days gone by, are currently fuelling my creative fire. Today I’m sharing the classic children’s book “There was an old lady who swallowed a fly” illustrated by the incredible Pam Adams. First published in 1973, this is a much loved classic with ingenious die-cut holes that bring this well-known nursery rhyme to life. I love Pam Adams' work. Her illustrations are so humorous and vibrant, and I can’t get enough of that psychedelic colour palette! Only problem is my son’s getting a bit old for this one now. Guess I’ll just have to read it on my own.

item.title: Rick Hyde - PencilBooth Take #2
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde

Welcome to Take #2 comrades, so glad you stuck around for more! I hope everyone is having a marvellous May, and is starting to see a bit more sunshine. I spent last Sunday in a beer garden here in Manchester, and it’s been a while since I’ve been able to say that! Anyway, I’ll stop prattling on about the weather (terribly British of me I know) and crack on with some updates!

Inkygoodness Community Badges

For those that don’t know, I’m a proud member of Inkygoodness, the global creative community run by the one and only Lisa Hassell. Over the last few weeks, we've been working together, creating some community badges to adorn members' profiles. We’ve been covering things like co-host, mentor and various awards, challenges and courses. It’s been a lot of fun, and it’s ace contributing to the community this way. There are more batches planned, so watch this space 👀 We can't wait to share them with you! Click here to find out more about Inkygoodness.

AGOG! Zine / Solar Power

And here’s an animation of a sun! Staying off the subject of weather didn’t last long did it. But hear me out. Last month I was invited to submit for issue 2 of AGOG! The Liverpool based Art & Illustration zine, founded by 3D artist Craig Boylan and illustrator Luke McConkey. I wanted to create something new, and with the changing of the seasons upon us I decide to go (you’ve guessed it) weather related. The work itself, is an attempt to convey the pure joy sunshine can bring. I was pretty chuffed with the character, and I couldn’t resist animating him. Looking forward to sharing the printed version soon! Click here to find out more about AGOG!

PencilBooth Promo

Here’s something else I made recently. Just a crazy little postman to promote this here newsletter. I hope you like him!

In Print

It’s always a buzz to see your work in print, and I finally got my hands on the latest issue of Fast Company magazine, featuring my spot illos for the cover story on Taco Bell CEO, Sean Tresvant. Thanks again to Alice Alves at Fast Company for bringing me on board. Click here to view the full project.

Spinspiration

Recently, I’ve been returning to a few old classics including this, Terry Callier's 'What Color Is Love’. It’s a melting pot of soul, funk, rock, folk and jazz, and a must have for any music aficionado. My personal favourite is the track ‘You Goin’ Miss Your Candyman’. I can happily draw to this album for hours on end. Stick it on loop and let the creative juices flow.

Eye Candy

We recently took a family trip to London, and it was my 5 year old son’s first time in the big smoke. As an introduction, a London based friend of mine sent him a reissue of Miroslav Šašek’s classic ‘This is London’. I’ve absolutely loved reading this with him. The amusing verse, coupled with Šašek’s bright and charming illustrations is infectious. They don’t make them like they used to!

item.title: Rick Hyde - PencilBooth Take #3
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde

Football fever is sweeping England, and everybody is boarding the hype train to the Euro 2024 final in Berlin. So it only seems fitting that this month’s take has a bit of a footie theme in parts. Yes, I’m celebrating the beautiful game with a tribute to Manchester United and Kobbie Mainoo, who is proving to be an absolute superstar in The Three Lion’s midfield. I mean, was there ever any doubt?

  In other news, I’m in the process of setting up an online shop. Hurrah! And in a beautiful twist of fate, all the images shared in this month’s newsletter will be available to buy as prints, once that’s up and running. Watch this space.

  And so, on with the news…

Kobbie Mainoo | Manchester United FA Cup Winners 2024 Poster

So, as promised here's Mr. Kobbie Mainoo, but not in his current England demeanour, but in his 2024 FA Cup Winning, Manchester United guise. Bucket hat and all.


As a life long Manchester United fan, I couldn’t resist paying homage to him after getting the winning goal in the FA Cup final. Hopefully he'll do the same on Sunday!

Click here to see the full project on my website >>

War On Robots

So this is a recent piece I made, addressing some of the fears surrounding AI within our industry at the moment. Whether you're an eager adopter or angry objector, there's no denying that this is a hot topic right now, and it isn't going away any time soon.

Get onboard or declare war? I think I might be fighting a loosing battle to be honest.

Click here to see the Instagram post, with detail and sketches included >>

Solar Power Print

Last month I shared the animated version of my submission for AGOG! The Liverpool based Art & Illustration zine, founded by 3D artist Craig Boylan and illustrator Luke McConkey. Well this is the original artwork, and another print I plan to make available in my forthcoming shop.


I hope you like my sun character as much as I enjoyed making him. Fingers crossed, he’s not the only sun we’re going to see in the UK this summer!


Click here to see the Instagram post, with detail and sketches included >>

Stick It To The ‘Gram

Staying with the AI theme, last month there was a bit of a revolt from illustrators on Instagram, responding to concerns around Meta’s stance on artificial intelligence. This saw a mass migration to Cara, an app that offers an alternative to Instagram, but solely focused on artists. Cara is explicitly against AI art, and more specifically, the ethical and data privacy issues surrounding it.

I was swept up with the mob, and promptly set up an account on there. However, since the initial frenzy, the buzz appears to be waning. Nevertheless, I think it's still a cool place for creatives to hang out, and will be continuing to contribute and support the community on there.

Find me on Cara here >>

item.title: Rick Hyde - Festive Sign Off
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde

Hi gang, I just wanted to wish everyone a Very Merry Christmas, before I sign off for the year. Much like a Christmas chocolate selection box, my 2024 has been a bit of a mixed bag. The year has not been without its challenges, but I’ve also worked on some really fun projects with some really great people. I hope 2025 brings more of that for us all. So without further ado, I’ll employ a criminally overused seasonal pun, and wrap things up!

Joy • Love • Peace

Wishing you all joy, love and peace this Christmas! A little festive illustration I made in Womp recently. After much encouragement from some 3D illustrator pals, I finally gave Womp a go, and I love it! For those that don’t know, Womp is beginner-friendly, browser based, 3D modelling software. I’ve had loads of fun playing with the app over the last couple of weeks, and I'm very keen to learn more 3D in 2025. Watch this space…

For 3D video animations, vector artwork and sketch, check out the post on Instagram.

View on Instagram

100 Rejections Challenge

Last week saw the end of the Inkygoodness Collective 100 Rejections Challenge, and to mark the occasion, I took to Womp again. I decided to recreate a 3D version of the badge I designed earlier this year, and was really happy with the result. I think it’s added an extra dimension to my work. What do you reckon folks?


For 3D video animations, alternative renders, vector artwork and sketch, check out the post on Instagram.

View on Instagram

The Rizz Biz

I’d had my eye on True Grit Texture Supply’s RizzCraft Risograph Effects Brushes for a while, and finally decided to try them out the other week. I call this one Tree Hugger, and it’s inspired by the leafy Manchester suburb of Whalley Range, where I live. I’ve always loved the Risograph aesthetic, and I think these brushes do a pretty good job of recreating it. I totally recommend giving them a go if you love a bit of rizz!


For close-ups, vector artwork and sketch, check out the post on Instagram.

View on Instagram
https://www.cartoonsaloon.ie/song-of-the-sea/
Song of the Sea - Cartoon Saloon |

A beautiful animation I saw recently from 2014. Currently on Netflix.

https://womp.com/
Womp: Free 3D design software
https://margoguryan.bandcamp.com/album/take-a-picture
Take A Picture, by Margo Guryan

My current obsession.

https://www.truegrittexturesupply.com/products/rizzcraft?variant=44250297499834
RizzCraft

Well, that’s it from me.

I hope you had loads of successes in 2024, and wish you many more for 2025.

Thanks for all the support and encouragement this year.

Hi folks, I hope all’s good. Just checking in with a few updates as we head into spring.

Stretford Shindig

This is a poster I created for an upcoming event, called The Great Big Stretford Shindig.

The night is to be held at Stretford Public Hall in Manchester, on Saturday May 10th (6-11pm).

It’s a fundraiser for a close friend, whose world was turned upside down last year by a cancer diagnosis. The treatment she needs is not available through the NHS, so all proceeds will help fund her life-saving treatment.

Range Life is an idea for a clothing brand, inspired by the leafy Manchester suburb of Whalley Range, where I live.

item.title: The Music Issue
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde

Hi Folks. Thought I'd check in and share some recent updates from the past few months. If you're curious about what I’ve been up to, read on. Spoiler alert, there’s music in this one.

Ted Lucas Album Artwork

The start of the Summer saw me taking on a new personal project, and real labour of love. It was a redesign of the album artwork for Ted Lucas’ 1975 cult classic self-titled album “Ted Lucas”. I discovered the album earlier this year, and it quickly became one of my all time favourites. To discover more about this mythical album, and the inspiration behind my redesign, click the link below.

Find out more

Oasis Fan Art

Here’s a nod to one of my all-time favourite bands from the ‘90s. Oasis might not be to everyone’s taste, but their influence on British music and culture is hard to ignore. That legacy was on full display recently as they kicked off The Oasis Live '25 Tour right here in Manchester, and Oasis mania swept the city.

I was fully onboard the hype train, and bagged a ticket for one of the Heaton Park gigs. To see more on this artwork, and other snaps from the day, click the link below.

View on Instagram

Bananagun Album Artwork

To round out this trio of music projects, here’s one more. This design comes from a recent proposal I put together for one of my favourite record labels, Full Time Hobby, and their artist Bananagun. Their sunshine pop felt like a natural fit for my style, so I explored some early ideas for album artwork and merch. You can see more from the project over on Instagram.

View on Instagram

Studio Noel Interview

Back in April, I had a chat with the folks at Studio Noel for their Creative Conversations series. We covered a bit of everything, from the creative process to finding inspiration. Click the link below for the full interview.

Read the interview

Inkygoodness Badges - Batch 3

Over the past few years I’ve loved working with the Inkygoodness creative community. In April, I designed their new Points & Recognition Badges, plus a few fresh Challenge Badges. See the results on Instagram.

View on Instagram

Pdf Portfolio

I also took some time this spring to update my PDF portfolio, something I share with prospective clients when I’m looking for new projects. It’s a useful way to take stock, reflect on progress, and spot areas for growth. Feel free to take a look via the link below.

View my pdf portfolio

Showreel 2025

April also saw me update my motion showreel. I still animate as much as I illustrate (I started in Flash in the early 2000s). I’m always open to motion design projects, so drop me a line if anything’s brewing.

View my showreel

Logo Reel

I’ve always enjoyed animating logos, and recently curated a short reel of my favourite pieces, complete with sound effects. Why not give it a watch?

View my logo reel

That’s it from me for now.

Hope you’ve enjoyed the update, and wherever summer takes you, I hope it’s a good one.
I’ll be back in a month or two with more to share.

Take it easy folks,
Rick

item.title: BRIT the North | The BRITs Art Trail
item.ns0:encoded:
From Sketch to Billboard: BRIT the North

It’s been a little while since my last newsletter, September in fact. Thank you for sticking around.

I wanted to share a recent project I’m proud to be part of: BRIT the North, created for The BRITs Art Trail in Manchester.

As part of Manchester Welcomes… The BRITs 2026, The BRITs Art Trail transforms the Northern Quarter and Ancoats into a citywide open-air gallery from 12 February to 16 March.

Curated by Stanley Chow, in collaboration with Sony Music and Bandwagon, and produced by Wild in Art, the trail features 21 North-West artists responding to the question:

What do The BRITs and the music of 2025 mean to you?

Here’s how I answered it.

The Sketch

This initial sketch was about finding the right balance between references to The BRITs, my personal highlights from the music of 2025, and Manchester’s cultural legacy.

The Artwork

The piece brings together favourite BRITs memories, selected nominees from the 2025 shortlist, and a tribute to Manchester’s iconic artists, venues and labels.

2026 nominees from Sony Music and affiliated labels are also woven throughout the composition.

The Billboard

BRIT the North on display at New Islington Marina.

Seeing it up on the billboard, out in the city that inspired it, felt special.

Photograph by Ellen Offredy.

The Trail

The official BRITs Art Trail poster, designed by Stanley Chow, alongside my billboard.

The trail runs across the Northern Quarter and Ancoats, turning everyday spaces into an open-air gallery.

Photograph by Ellen Offredy.

Artist and Plaque

With the work at New Islington Marina.

It’s been a great experience exhibiting alongside such talented North-West artists. Thank you to Stan Chow, Beth Parnell and Ben Reed for bringing me on board and making it happen.

Find Out More

If you’re in Manchester before 16 March, the trail is well worth exploring in person.
You can discover all the artists and locations here.

And If you’d like to talk about a project, collaboration, or just say hello, please feel free to get in touch.

Thanks for reading.
Rick

item.title: Rick Hyde x Lucy & Yak
item.ns0:encoded:
Rick Hyde x Lucy & Yak

Hi folks.

It's been a few months since I last dropped into your inbox, so I thought it was about time I gave you an update.

I've had various bits and bobs on, but there's one project in particular I'd like to share with you today.

Back at the end of July, Lucy & Yak were looking for a local artist to collaborate with on their new Manchester store. When they asked if I’d be interested, it didn't take long for me to say YES!

The project saw me creating a series of colourful, character-led pieces bringing together vibrant, psychedelic illustrations with Lucy & Yak’s positive and inclusive ethos. Artworks were produced for the shopfront, illuminated lightboxes, exclusive merchandise, and a collection of embroidery and patch designs for the store opening.

Below, I’ll share all those elements in a bit more detail.

So strap yourself in and slap on your shades, because it's about to get BRIGHT in here 🌟

Storefront

The storefront artwork was designed as a psychedelic explosion of colour and joy, full of energy, with a proper sense of Manchester running through it. There are references throughout, from Frank Sidebottom to The Happy Mondays, alongside broader nods to the city’s rich musical and footballing heritage. All of this is interwoven with Lucy & Yak’s positivity, inclusivity and celebration of individuality.

Lightboxes

Inside the store, I created two lightbox designs, extending the visual language of the storefront into the interior. Both pieces build on the community feeling developed in the storefront artwork, combining colourful characters in the local settings of Alexandra Park and the Manchester Ship Canal.

Merchandise

The collaboration also extended into a limited-edition tote bag and T-shirt, which is available exclusively from the Manchester store. Both designs bring the same psychedelic energy and community feeling to wearable and everyday pieces.

Patches & Embroidery

For the store opening, I created a collection of small embroidery patch designs, simplifying existing artwork from the wider project. These were brought to life by the brilliant Re:Yak Studio team. I also created embroidery flash sheets, giving customers the chance to stitch my artwork onto patches themselves.

If you've made it this far, thanks for reading. You're a true legend!

I'll be back in a month or so with another quick round-up.

So until then, take it dungareasy.

Rick x
